findings.explanation: All antecedents of the HOL4 theorem are missing: `q has_type Bool`, `term_ok (sigof thy) q`, the semantic premise over structures `i`, `v`, and `(thy,h1) |= p1`, `(thy,h2) |= p2`. Only `is_set_theory mem` remains, and `p1`, `p2` do not occur in the conclusion. Lean therefore asserts that every theory, with any hypotheses, entails every term. This is false: for q = `Abs (Const n ty) p`, `entails0` requires `has_type q BoolTy`, which is underivable (likewise any thy that is not `theory_ok`). With `is_set_theory mem` it proves False, so the statement is strictly stronger than HOL4's true conditional rule.
findings.repair:
theorem binary_inference_rule [Nonempty U] (mem : U → U → Prop) :
    is_set_theory mem →
      ∀ (thy : thy) (h1 h2 : List term) (p1 p2 q : term),
        has_type q BoolTy ∧ term_ok (sigof thy) q ∧
        (∀ (i : interpretation U) (v : valuation U),
          is_structure0 mem (sigof thy) i v ∧
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v p1 = true_ mem ∧
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v p2 = true_ mem →
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v q = true_ mem) ∧
        entails0 mem (thy, h1) p1 ∧ entails0 mem (thy, h2) p2 →
        entails0 mem (thy, term_union h1 h2) q := by sorry
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSoundness

namespace Candle

open HOL Classical

example {U : Type} [Nonempty U] (mem : U → U → Prop) (hs : is_set_theory mem)
    (P : type_of% (binary_inference_rule mem))
    (t : thy) (n : mlstring) (ty : type) (p : term) : False := by
  have h := P hs t [] [] p p (Abs (Const n ty) p)
  unfold entails0 at h
  have h1 := h.2.2.1
  simp only [EVERY] at h1
  have h2 : has_type (Abs (Const n ty) p) BoolTy := h1.1
  cases h2

end Candle
findings.hol4_check: ¬(∀(thy:thy) h1 h2 q. entails0 (m:'U->'U->bool) (thy,term_union h1 h2) q)
